replacements.old: - [ ] Prove that prediction alone is insufficient for general intelligence by constructing same-predictive/different-control-relevance examples.
replacements.new: - [x] Prove that prediction alone is insufficient for general intelligence by constructing same-predictive/different-control-relevance examples. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae7-prediction-to-control-v1` PC-1: two sensors with **identical predictive content** — equal block masses and equal conditional laws, cell by cell as exact rationals, for **every** one of the 6 registered targets, so no predictor under any loss can tell them apart — have control values `1` and `1/2` under `U_hidden_coordinate`, a gap of exactly `1/2`. Over the full census of **4140** sensors (**712** distinct predictive profiles) there are **10,980** such same-predictive/different-control pairs; the contrast is reported too — under `U_visible_coordinate`, whose optima are measurable in the registered targets, the count is exactly **0**. The claim is scoped to the registered target suite and utility family, and `PREDICTION_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_INTELLIGENCE_IN_GENERAL` is a registered forbidden promotion.

replacements.old: - [ ] Formalize control-relevant sufficient state / action equivalence under a utility or behavioral specification.
replacements.new: - [x] Formalize control-relevant sufficient state / action equivalence under a utility or behavioral specification. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae7-prediction-to-control-v1` PC-2: `T` is control-sufficient iff `V(T) = V_full` with `V` exact rational; **225 / 225 / 208 / 221** of the 4140 sensors are control-sufficient for the four registered utilities, and the **coarsest** such sensor is computed by exhaustive minimisation rather than asserted — it is unique for two utilities and **not** unique for the other two (**3** and **8** minimal elements, all reported). The action-equivalence criterion — a block is free iff its states share an optimal action — matches the exact value function on **every** pairwise merge, **0** mismatches across all four utilities, and is proved **not** to be a pairwise-local property: **1** triple `(0,1,2)` is pairwise compatible yet has empty common optimum, so Helly fails and a pairwise checker is unsound.

replacements.old: - [ ] Relate to POMDP belief states, sufficient information states, rate-distortion control and bounded rationality; subtract parent mathematics.
replacements.new: - [x] Relate to POMDP belief states, sufficient information states, rate-distortion control and bounded rationality; subtract parent mathematics. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae7-prediction-to-control-v1` PC-3: a machine-readable crosswalk of **5** entries, each carrying a DOI — belief-state sufficiency (Åström 1965, doi:10.1016/0022-247X(65)90154-X; Smallwood & Sondik 1973, doi:10.1287/opre.21.5.1071), MDP bisimulation/model minimisation (Givan, Dean & Greig 2003, doi:10.1016/S0004-3702(02)00376-4), rate-distortion control and information-theoretic bounded rationality (Tishby & Polani 2011, doi:10.1007/978-1-4419-1452-1_19; Ortega & Braun 2013, doi:10.1098/rspa.2012.0683), value of information (Howard 1966, doi:10.1109/TSSC.1966.300074) and rational inattention (Sims 2003, doi:10.1016/S0304-3932(03)00029-1). **3** entries terminate `PARENT_SUFFICIENT`, recorded as successes; the named residual is the exhaustive 4140-sensor census with counts in both directions and the priced ladder.

replacements.old: - [ ] Derive value-of-information conditions for when sensing/remembering/computing additional information is worth its resource cost.
replacements.new: - [x] Derive value-of-information conditions for when sensing/remembering/computing additional information is worth its resource cost. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae7-prediction-to-control-v1` PC-4: acquire the finer sensor iff `VoI(T,T') > price · (cost(T) − cost(T'))`. Over **163,754** comparable sensor pairs, **26,790** have value of information exactly `0` and **136,964** strictly positive, and the exact break-even prices form **71** distinct rationals spanning `0` to `9/64`. The full-versus-blind probe has `VoI = 9/64` over a cost increment of `7`, break-even `9/448`: strictly below it the fine sensor wins (`85/128` vs `71/128`), **at** it the two are exactly tied (`71/128` vs `71/128`) — the tie is reported, not skipped — and strictly above it the blind sensor wins (`57/128` vs `71/128`).

replacements.old: - [ ] Derive when an agent should compress observations more aggressively because actions are insensitive to distinctions.
replacements.new: - [x] Derive when an agent should compress observations more aggressively because actions are insensitive to distinctions. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae7-prediction-to-control-v1` PC-5: merging a set of states costs no control value **iff** the intersection of their optimal-action sets is non-empty. The criterion is verified against the exact value function on every one of the **28** pairwise merges for each utility — **0** mismatches — and is non-vacuous in both directions: **12 / 12 / 13 / 14** free pairs against **16 / 16 / 15 / 14** costly ones for the four registered utilities.

replacements.old: - [ ] Derive when control requires preserving distinctions that pure prediction would discard.
replacements.new: - [x] Derive when control requires preserving distinctions that pure prediction would discard. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae7-prediction-to-control-v1` PC-6, the exact converse of PC-5: **4** state pairs are invisible to **all 6** registered targets, and **4 of 4** of them are strictly control-relevant under `U_hidden_coordinate` — merging `{0,4}` drops `V` from `1` to `7/8` — while under `U_visible_coordinate` the count is exactly **0**. The boundary of the witness is measured rather than hidden: adding `Y_b2` or `Y_parity` destroys the redundancy entirely (**0** surviving pairs), but adding `Y_majority` does **not** — **2** pairs survive, because on the four states with `b0 = b1` the majority is pinned by `b0`.

replacements.old: - [ ] Prospectively predict policy/representation transitions under changing information-processing prices.
replacements.new: - [x] Prospectively predict policy/representation transitions under changing information-processing prices. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae7-prediction-to-control-v1` PC-7: five predictions `R1`–`R5` were written into `FREEZE_V1.md` at commit `65b45210` **before** any executor, oracle or receipt blob existed, and **all five HELD**. `R1` monotone coarsening: **0** nesting violations over 33 price points × 4 problems. `R2`: **2** problems show ≥3 distinct selected sensors. `R3`: **0** transitions fall outside the **121**-element exact set of difference quotients `(V(T)−V(T'))/(cost(T)−cost(T'))`. `R4`: **0** failures — above the maximal gain the blind sensor is selected everywhere. `R5`: **4 of 4** problems select a control-sufficient sensor that is **not** predictively sufficient for some registered target, so the priced control order is not the predictive order. The ladder is proved non-vacuous (every problem moves, two move three times).

replacements.old: - [ ] Prove that observational compression/prediction does not generally identify causal structure.
replacements.new: - [x] Prove that observational compression/prediction does not generally identify causal structure. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae13-causality-intervention-v1` CI-1: over the complete census of **547,625** SCMs — all **25** labelled DAGs on three binary variables, every CPT drawn from the frozen grid `{0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1}` — the 25 DAGs fall into **11** Markov equivalence classes, and **all 7** classes containing more than one DAG carry an exhibited witness: two parameterisations of **different** DAGs whose observational joints agree on **all 8 atoms** as exact rationals and whose interventional answers differ. **80,788,144** such cross-DAG disagreeing pairs exist over **26,601** joints realised by two or more DAGs of one class. The quantifier is kept: the **4** singleton classes **are** identified, and they are reported with count `0` rather than omitted — the claim is *not generally identified*, never *never identified*.

replacements.old: - [ ] Construct observationally equivalent worlds with different intervention consequences.
replacements.new: - [x] Construct observationally equivalent worlds with different intervention consequences. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae13-causality-intervention-v1` CI-2: `A → C` against `C → A` with `B` isolated, `P(A=1) = 1/2`, `P(C=1|A=1) = 3/4`, `P(C=1|A=0) = 1/4`. The observational joint `(3/16, 1/16, 3/16, 1/16, 1/16, 3/16, 1/16, 3/16)` sums exactly to `1` and is reproduced by exactly **1** parameterisation of the other DAG, found by exhaustive search over the frozen grid. The registered answers then separate completely: `ACE_A_on_C` is `1/2` under one member and `0` under the other, `ACE_C_on_A` is `0` and `1/2` — the identification interval of each is the full `[0, 1/2]` while the observational joint is identical cell by cell.

replacements.old: - [ ] Define when interventions are required for the behavioral specification.
replacements.new: - [x] Define when interventions are required for the behavioral specification. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae13-causality-intervention-v1` CI-3: interventions are required for a specification `(query, tolerance)` **iff** the half-width of that query's identification interval over the observational equivalence class exceeds the tolerance. The rule is tested on both sides and **at** the boundary: with worst-case half-width `1/2`, at tolerance `31/64` interventions are required, at exactly `1/2` they are **not**, and at `33/64` they are not — the flip is verified at the exact rational threshold rather than sampled around it. Per query, **5,356** of **26,601** joint groups have a non-degenerate interval and **21,245** are identified observationally; the four registered queries give identical counts, as the relabelling symmetry of the full census forces.

replacements.old: - [ ] Derive the value of intervention under resource cost.
replacements.new: - [x] Derive the value of intervention under resource cost. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae13-causality-intervention-v1` CI-4: the value of an atomic intervention is exactly half the identification-interval width, since the experiment answers its own query exactly; acquire iff that exceeds the price. The worst case over the census is `1/2`. Intervention is **not** universally worth its cost, and this is exhibited rather than conceded: **84,980** query-group specifications have value of intervention exactly `0`, and a named one is carried in the receipt — `ACE_C_on_A` on a joint realised by all **25** DAGs, identified answer `0`, interval width `0`.

replacements.old: - [ ] Distinguish predictive state from causal/control state.
replacements.new: - [x] Distinguish predictive state from causal/control state. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae13-causality-intervention-v1` CI-5: on the registered confounded subfamily `B → A`, `B → C`, `A → C`, the predictive state (the partition of the four `(A,B)` contexts by `p(C=1|A,B)`) and the causal/control state (the partition by the full interventional response vector `(p(C=1|do(A=0)), p(C=1|do(A=1)))` at that context) are different objects: over the **2,187** strictly positive models (**75,938** excluded for a zero atom, reported not dropped) the relation is `INCOMPARABLE` **1,458** times, `PREDICTIVE_STRICTLY_REFINES` **486**, `EQUAL` **243**, and `CAUSAL_STRICTLY_REFINES` **0** — the last a **proved** zero, not an unobserved one: the causal state separates only the two values of the context, so for it to refine the predictive partition strictly the predictive partition would have to be trivial, and then the causal one is trivial too and the relation is `EQUAL`.

replacements.old: - [ ] Relate to causal-state, causal-representation-learning and causal-inference parents precisely.
replacements.new: - [x] Relate to causal-state, causal-representation-learning and causal-inference parents precisely. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae13-causality-intervention-v1` CI-6: **6** crosswalk entries, each with a citation — truncated factorisation and do-calculus (Pearl 1995, doi:10.1093/biomet/82.4.669; Pearl 2009, doi:10.1017/CBO9780511803161), Markov equivalence (Verma & Pearl 1990; Andersson, Madigan & Perlman 1997, doi:10.1214/aos/1031833662), partial identification (Balke & Pearl 1997, doi:10.1080/01621459.1997.10474074), experimental design (Hauser & Bühlmann 2014, doi:10.1111/rssb.12071), causal representation learning (Schölkopf et al. 2021, doi:10.1109/JPROC.2021.3058954) — with **3** `PARENT_SUFFICIENT` terminals recorded as successes. The entry that matters most is the sixth: the computational-mechanics `causal state` (Shalizi & Crutchfield 2001, doi:10.1023/A:1010388907793) is a **purely predictive** equivalence class of histories with no interventional content and is **not** the Pearlian causal structure; `COMPUTATIONAL_MECHANICS_CAUSAL_STATE_IS_PEARLIAN_CAUSAL_STATE` is a registered forbidden promotion and CI-5 measures how far apart the two notions actually sit.
